method: Independent analytic derivation with numerical checks, separate from rendered labels
claims: Parallel sunlight illuminates a hemisphere of the ideal sphere outside eclipses. The view from Earth reveals the intersection with the visible hemisphere; phases follow changing Sun-Moon-observer angle.

With orbital elongation alpha in the simple distant-Sun model, projected illuminated disk fraction is (1-cos alpha)/2. The terminator projects to x=sign(sin alpha) cos alpha sqrt(1-y squared); its edge-on view is a diameter. The scene renders binary illuminated area, not photometric brightness.

Real lunar orbit tilt avoids monthly eclipses; ordinary phases are not Earth shadows. Synodic cycle approximately 29.5 days from NASA/USNO source. Orientation is illustrative, not a time/location-specific sky prediction.

checks.description: Independent strip-area integral matches phase fraction
Quarter has half projected area and full has all projected area
Terminator projects to a diameter at quarter

limitations: Numerical samples check implementations; general conclusions rest on the stated mathematical arguments.
